SALES HANDOFF

One sales process.
Two people who can run it.

Your sales process includes who you target, how you reach them, what you ask on calls, and how you move a deal to signature. In a founder-led company, much of that is known only to the founder. Antaeus records it as you work, inside the same product areas you already use: the accounts you track, where every deal actually stands, the discovery questions that led to a second meeting, and pilot results. There is no separate documentation step. When your first go-to-market hire starts, you share the handoff kit with them, and they read that context themselves instead of relying on you to explain it from memory.

Antaeus uses language models to analyze workspace data and draft text. We do not market Antaeus by which model it uses. Generated text follows the same writing rules as the rest of Antaeus, and the interface shows the source data behind each analysis.

Pain & consequence · live Walk me through what happens the week a new store opens. Listen for whether the buyer owns the problem and who is accountable for its cost. “It is messy but we cope” “We just hired two more recruiters” “Not a top priority” They added recruiters instead of changing the underlying process. Ask what the added headcount cost and who approved the expense; that identifies the budget owner. Discovery. Use the console during the live call. It shows the current question and what to listen for. Select the buyer response you heard; Antaeus shows the recommended follow-up and offers a jump to where the conversation went.

Is this a CRM? No. A CRM primarily stores activity and pipeline data for reporting. Antaeus ranks next actions and shows the reason behind each ranking. It does not include team territories, quotas across a team, admin roles, or forecast rollups. If those are your primary needs, use a CRM.

What does setup actually involve? About one afternoon. Setup asks for the judgment only you have: who you actually sell to, the companies you are pursuing, and where each active deal really stands — the champion, who signs, and what it is stuck on. Antaeus is most useful with at least ten active deals; with fewer, setup tells you plainly that the picture will stay thin.Antaeus finds recent public events for each company and can look up industry, size, and location. You enter the private sales context it cannot find.

Why does it ask for so much up front? Because the most important deal context cannot be imported: why a deal is stuck, why a past win worked, and who actually decides. Only you know it. Antaeus asks for that judgment once during setup, then uses it in every account, deal, and action recommendation after. We ask for it up front and say so, instead of hiding it behind a short form and giving you shallow recommendations.

Do I need a sales team for this to make sense? No. Antaeus is designed for the period when the founder is still selling and the first serious go-to-market hire has not started yet or has just started. An established sales organization has different needs and better-suited tools.

How is it different from the tools I already turned down? Many alternatives are databases with chat interfaces. A useful test is whether the product ranks one next action and explains why that one comes first, or only shows a list for you to sort yourself. Antaeus ranks actions, shows its reasoning, and lets you disagree with the recommendation.

Does it send emails or make calls for me? No. Antaeus drafts outreach and call language, but you send messages through your existing email tools. If you BCC a capture address and connect your calendar link, Antaeus counts sends and meetings with the accounts you track. It does not place calls or contact buyers on its own.

What does "ready to hand off" actually mean? It means a person who starts Monday could run your sales process without you sitting next to them. Antaeus answers that with a state, not a score: you are the system, then building, then inheritable with guardrails (a hire could run it with you there to answer questions), then hire-ready, and finally hire-ready, repeatable once you have won and lost enough deals to see the pattern. Each state has conditions you can read, and Antaeus shows what it would take to reach the next one.
Is it using AI? Yes. Antaeus uses language models to analyze workspace data, detect changes, and draft text. You are paying for the ranking and the recorded sales context, not for a particular model.

What happens to what I put in? It stays yours. You can export your accounts, deals, calls, pilots, and plans as one file, restore a copy, or delete them after a typed confirmation. Antaeus does not sell your workspace data or use your accounts and deals to train public models.
What will it cost? Nothing while we're in beta, and no card to start. When there is a price it will be posted plainly on this page before it applies to anyone already using it.

WRITING TO LENA, HEAD OF PEOPLE AT CHOMPS

Lena — I saw Chomps announce two new plants.

That will require several hundred production hires on a deadline, and from the outside it looks like the people team will absorb most of the load. Screening is often the first bottleneck.

Worth twenty minutes next week to compare how you are staffing the openings?

Why now
Two plants · small recruiting team
The ask
20 minutes next week
Copy the message

Open the call
Why it matters to them

THEY WILL PROBABLY SAY

“We are too small for something like this.”

Small teams feel a bad hire hardest. Ask what one unsuccessful store-manager hire cost them last year. A number the buyer says out loud is hard to argue with.

Review before you dial · log the outcome after · never during the call

Cold call. Review the call structure, likely buyer objections, and recommended responses before you dial. Log the outcome after the call, not while speaking.
